The show's revolutionary format remains as relevant and powerful as ever, proving its staying power nearly a decade after its debut.

Among newer productions, **Maybe Happy Ending** stands out as a critical darling, scoring 85/100 across 34 reviews. This charming robot love story has captured critics' attention as one of Broadway's most original musicals in recent years, offering audiences something genuinely fresh. Meanwhile, **Oh, Mary!** delivers absurdist comedy with Cole Escola's riotous take on Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, cabaret-obsessed narcissist, earning an 84/100 and proving that bold, unconventional approaches can thrive on Broadway.

With an average critical score of 74 out of 100 across these five productions, the season delivers solid theatrical craftsmanship, if not universal acclaim. best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted. These productions debuted in the brief window before the pandemic shuttered theaters that March, making them among the last shows to premiere before Broadway's historic 18-month closure.

The strongest survivor from this cohort is **Les Misérables**, which scores 82/100 from critics for its grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This reimagined production strips away some of the original's spectacle in favor of a rawer, more intimate approach that has won over most reviewers, though purists remain divided on the radical changes.

**A Soldier's Play** stands as another critical highlight, earning 78/100 for bringing Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway for the first time. The production's examination of racism within a 1940s Army regiment resonates powerfully in contemporary context, with critics praising the ensemble's stellar performances and the play's continued relevance.

The remaining shows present more mixed results. Laura Linney's solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton** showcases virtuosic acting in service of Elizabeth Strout's intimate novel, while **Grand Horizons** offers well-acted but conventional comedy. Ivo van Hove's **West Side Story** proves the most polarizing, with its experimental approach earning both passionate advocates and fierce detractors.

With an average score of 74/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 demonstrates solid craftsmanship even as it reflects a theatrical landscape on the cusp of unprecedented change. For theatergoers interested in Broadway history, these shows represent the last gasp of the pre-pandemic era.

Close behind, Rebecca Frecknall's immersive reimagining of "Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club" earns widespread acclaim for its stunning transformation of the Playhouse Theatre into a fully realized nightclub environment.

Epic dramas such as "The Lehman Trilogy" share space with intimate solo performances like "Lackawanna Blues," while revivals including Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped "Company" prove that classic material can be vitally reimagined for contemporary audiences.

Whether you're drawn to innovative theatrical forms, spectacular musical productions, or powerful dramatic storytelling, these productions from Broadway's reopening year continue to define what made that moment so special. best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted—productions that launched just before or during one of the most tumultuous periods in theatrical history. Despite the challenges, several shows from this season have left lasting impressions on critics and continue to resonate with audiences.

Leading our rankings is a reimagined **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 82/100 from critics who largely embrace its grittier approach to the classic material, though the production remains divisive for some traditionalists. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** stands as a triumph at 78/100, with Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally receiving its long-overdue Broadway debut in a revival that critics hail as both stellar and urgently relevant.

The season also showcases notable experiments in theatrical form. **My Name is Lucy Barton** features Laura Linney in a solo adaptation of Elizabeth Strout's novel that divides critics even as they universally praise Linney's performance. Meanwhile, **West Side Story** arrives in Ivo van Hove's radical reimagining—a polarizing production that earns either passionate praise for its bold vision or criticism for its departures from tradition.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the 2020 season demonstrates Broadway's enduring commitment to both classic revivals and fresh interpretations, even amid unprecedented circumstances. Whether you're drawn to socially conscious drama, intimate character studies, or daring directorial visions, these productions offer multiple entry points into the year's theatrical conversation.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As Broadway looks back from March 2026, the shows that opened in 2021 represent a remarkable chapter in theater history—the season when stages reopened after an unprecedented shutdown. Five years later, these productions continue to resonate as testaments to the art form's resilience and innovation.

The ten highest-rated plays from 2021 average an impressive 81/100 critical score, spanning experimental docudramas to beloved mega-musicals. Leading the pack is "Dana H.," Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance that critics describe as mesmerizing and unforgettable. Close behind, Rebecca Frecknall's immersive reimagining of "Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club" earns widespread acclaim for its stunning transformation of the Playhouse Theatre into a pre-war Berlin nightclub.

The diversity of this list reflects Broadway's breadth: "The Phantom of the Opera" proves that Andrew Lloyd Webber's spectacular mega-musical endures despite its camp, while intimate solo performances like Ruben Santiago-Hudson's "Lackawanna Blues" demonstrate theater's power to transport audiences through one performer's virtuosity. Sam Mendes' "The Lehman Trilogy" stands as an epic theatrical triumph, and Tina Satter's "Is This a Room" transforms a verbatim FBI transcript into gripping drama.

Gender-swapped revivals ("Company"), urgent contemporary works ("Pass Over"), exuberant pop musicals ("SIX"), and warm workplace comedies ("Clyde's") round out a season that showcased every facet of theatrical storytelling.

Whether you're discovering these productions for the first time or revisiting favorites from Broadway's historic reopening, this guide offers a comprehensive look at 2021's most critically acclaimed plays.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a remarkable period of artistic achievement, marked by an impressive concentration of Pulitzer Prize-winning works and critically acclaimed revivals that continue to resonate with audiences.

The season's standout is **Kimberly Akimbo**, David Lindsay-Abaire and Jeanine Tesori's quirky musical about a teenage girl with a rapid-aging condition, which critics consistently hail as a near-perfect balance of hilarious comedy and aching poignancy. Close behind are two equally celebrated productions: **Into the Woods**, a stripped-down Sondheim revival that serves as a fitting tribute to the late composer's genius, and **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's brazenly original meta-musical that earned both a Pulitzer Prize and widespread acclaim for its brutally honest exploration of Black queer identity.

What makes this season particularly noteworthy is the prominence of Pulitzer-winning dramas making their Broadway debuts or returns. Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog** crackles with renewed vitality, while Stephen Adly Guirgis's **Between Riverside and Crazy**, Paula Vogel's **How I Learned to Drive**, and Martyna Majok's **Cost of Living** all bring their award-winning insights to the Broadway stage. Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt** adds to this literary weight with a haunting meditation on Jewish identity and the Holocaust.

The collection also showcases bold new voices like Jordan E. Cooper's provocative satire **Ain't No Mo'** and the intimate storytelling mastery of Mike Birbiglia in **The Old Man & The Pool**.

With an average critic score of 83/100 across these ten productions, the 2022 season represents a high-water mark for thoughtful, challenging theater that rewards both first-time viewers and those seeking a second look.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2023

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that premiered in 2023 represent one of the most critically acclaimed seasons in recent memory, with an average critic score of 82/100 across our featured productions.

The year's theatrical landscape was defined by several triumphant revivals that proved classic works could speak powerfully to contemporary audiences. Maria Friedman's staging of **Merrily We Roll Along** leads our rankings, finally vindicating Sondheim's notorious 1981 flop with an emotionally resonant production that critics embraced wholeheartedly. **Parade** similarly found urgent new relevance in its revival, with Ben Platt and Micaela Diamond delivering powerhouse performances in this timely examination of prejudice and injustice.

New works also made their mark, with Branden Jacobs-Jenkins' **Appropriate** emerging as a searing family drama that critics hailed as a modern masterpiece, anchored by Sarah Paulson's blistering performance. The play's unflinching examination of inherited racism and family dysfunction struck a powerful chord with audiences and reviewers alike. Meanwhile, **Stereophonic**, despite opening late in the year with limited initial reviews, quickly built momentum as an immersive rock studio drama that critics called near-perfect.

The season also showcased Broadway's increasing genre diversity, from Alex Edelman's brilliant solo show **Just for Us** to the West End import **Stranger Things: The First Shadow**, which proved that technically stunning spectacle could coexist with substantive storytelling.

Whether you're catching up on productions still running or exploring these shows through cast recordings and published scripts, these 2023 premieres offer a compelling snapshot of Broadway at its most artistically vital.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2024

As of March 2026, the best plays that opened on Broadway in 2024 continue to demonstrate the remarkable range and vitality of American theater. This curated selection of 10 productions maintains an impressive average critic score of 86/100, reflecting a particularly strong year for new work and revivals alike.

The standout arrival is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's acclaimed drama about a 1970s rock band in the studio, which critics have hailed as a theatrical marvel for its authentic depiction of the creative process. The production has earned 22 reviews and an 89/100 score, establishing itself as one of the year's most significant dramatic achievements. Meanwhile, **Operation Mincemeat**, the grassroots British sensation, has successfully made the leap to Broadway with an 88/100 rating, praised for its inventive energy and ensemble work. Cole Escola's **Oh, Mary!**—an irreverent farce reimagining Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, cabaret-obsessed narcissist—has become an unexpected phenomenon, earning dual entries in the top rankings with scores of 85/100 and 84/100 across different review periods.

The year also brought strong revivals, including George C. Wolfe's **Gypsy** starring Audra McDonald in a deeply moving interpretation of Mama Rose, and a lavish production of **Oliver!** that balances Dickensian darkness with Lionel Bart's beloved score. Quieter but equally powerful, Rachel Herzog's **Mary Jane** offers an intimate portrait of maternal devotion that has resonated deeply with audiences and critics alike.

Whether you're drawn to bold new voices or fresh takes on classics, these productions represent the best of what Broadway had to offer in 2024.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As Broadway moves into March 2026, the season's strongest plays—those that opened in 2025—continue to demonstrate the remarkable range and vitality of American theater. From classic revivals to bold new works, these productions have earned critical acclaim for their artistic ambition and emotional resonance.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons**, which earns widespread praise for its emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work. The Dutch director's stripped-down approach to Arthur Miller's classic proves that thoughtful reinvention can illuminate timeless material. Close behind, the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** reminds audiences and critics alike why this quirky musical became a beloved modern classic, with reviewers praising its airtight writing and tender humor.

The season also showcases impressive range: **Paddington The Musical** enchants with its remarkably lifelike bear puppet, described as a theatrical marvel; a West End transfer of **The Producers** delivers belly laughs and expert comic timing; and Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English** offers a smart, sensitive exploration of language and identity. Meanwhile, ambitious new works like **Liberation**—a feminist memory play—and **Dead Outlaw**, a darkly comic musical about outlaw Elmer McCurdy's bizarre afterlife, push theatrical boundaries in different directions.

With an average critic score of 85 out of 100 across these ten productions, the quality remains consistently high, whether audiences seek classic American drama, family-friendly spectacle, or provocative new voices. Browse the complete rankings below to find your next Broadway experience.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings a lean but intriguing start to the year for new Broadway plays, with just one production making its debut so far this season.

**Bug** stands as the sole entry, marking the long-awaited Broadway premiere of Tracy Letts' 1996 psychological thriller. Originally produced off-Broadway and later adapted into a 2006 film, the play finally arrives on the Great White Way nearly three decades after its initial writing. Critics respond with mostly positive reviews, awarding the production a solid 74/100 average across 35 reviews. The claustrophobic two-hander, which explores paranoia, conspiracy theories, and psychological deterioration in a seedy motel room, represents a darker, more experimental offering than typically dominates Broadway stages. While not reaching unanimous acclaim, the production demonstrates continued interest in Letts' provocative early work and Broadway's occasional willingness to embrace challenging material.

With only one new play opening through March, 2026 represents an unusually quiet start for Broadway drama. This sparse landscape contrasts sharply with recent seasons that have seen multiple play premieres by spring. The limited sample size makes it difficult to identify broader trends, though **Bug**'s arrival suggests programmers remain interested in revisiting significant works from recent theatrical history rather than focusing exclusively on world premieres.

As the season progresses into spring and summer, theatergoers and industry observers will be watching to see whether additional play productions emerge to fill out the 2026 roster and provide a more complete picture of Broadway's dramatic offerings for the year.
